name: Yoruba
about: A tonal language of south-west Nigeria with a rich tradition of praise poetry (oriki), proverbs and talking drums. Spoken by tens of millions of people.

name: Hausa
about: The trade language of the Sahel. Hausa is a first or second language for tens of millions of people and is heard on radio across West Africa.
phrases: Na yi farin cikin haɗuwa da kai
nah yee fah-REEN CHEE-keen hah-DOO-wah dah KAI

name: Igbo
about: Spoken in south-eastern Nigeria. Igbo is tonal, has many dialects, and is famous for its proverbs, which are said to be the palm oil with which words are eaten.
phrases: Obi dị m ụtọ ịhụ gị
o-BEE dee m oo-TAW ee-HOO gee

name: Swahili
about: A Bantu language with many Arabic loanwords, used as a shared language across East Africa. It is an official language of the African Union.

name: Zulu
about: isiZulu is the most widely spoken home language in South Africa. It is known for its clicks, its rich praise songs and the greeting Sawubona, meaning I see you.

name: Twi
about: A dialect of Akan spoken in southern Ghana. Twi is tied to Adinkra symbols, kente weaving and a day-name tradition where your name comes from your birth day.

name: Amharic
about: The working language of Ethiopia, written in the ancient Ge'ez script. Amharic belongs to the Semitic family, like Arabic and Hebrew. Shown here in Latin letters.

name: Xhosa
about: isiXhosa is known for its click sounds, written with the letters c, q and x. It is one of South Africa's official languages and the language of Nelson Mandela.

name: Shona
about: The main language of Zimbabwe, spoken by most of its people. Shona is the language of the builders of Great Zimbabwe and of the mbira thumb piano.

name: Wolof
about: The most widely spoken language in Senegal and a lingua franca in Dakar. Wolof has no grammatical gender and is famous in West African music and griot song.

name: Somali
about: A Cushitic language and the national language of Somalia, with a strong tradition of oral poetry. Somali has used a Latin alphabet since 1972.

name: Oromo
about: Afaan Oromoo is one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa and is written in a Latin alphabet. It is the language of the Oromo people and the gadaa system of governance.

name: Lingala
about: A Bantu language of the Congo River basin, spread by traders and music. Lingala is the language of Congolese rumba and soukous.

name: Kinyarwanda
about: The national language of Rwanda, spoken by almost everyone in the country. It is a Bantu language where greetings change with the time of day.

name: Luganda
about: The language of the Baganda people and the most widely spoken language in Uganda's capital, Kampala. Greetings in Luganda are warm and detailed.

name: Sesotho
about: The national language of Lesotho and one of South Africa's official languages. Sesotho is known for its proverbs, called maele, and the colourful Basotho blanket.
phrases: Hlooho ea ka e a opa
SHLO-ho eh-ah kah eh ah O-pah

name: Afrikaans
about: A language that grew in southern Africa from Dutch, shaped by Khoi, Malay and African influences. It is spoken by millions in South Africa and Namibia.
phrases: Hoe gaan dit met jou familie?
hoo khahn dit met yoh fah-MEE-lee

name: Setswana
about: The national language of Botswana, spoken in southern Africa. Setswana is a tonal Bantu language known for the greeting Dumela and its many proverbs.
phrases: Ke bua Setswana go le gonnye
keh BOO-ah seh-TSWAH-nah ho leh HON-nyeh
Ba lelapa la gago ba kae?
bah leh-LAH-pah lah HAH-ho bah KAI

name: Chichewa
about: The national language of Malawi, also spoken in Zambia and Mozambique, where it is called Nyanja. Chichewa is a Bantu language with a rich storytelling tradition.

name: Malagasy
about: The national language of Madagascar. It belongs to the Austronesian family, brought by settlers who crossed the Indian Ocean more than a thousand years ago.
